questions.question:
Identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Climate change are a greatest threat facing our planet which needs our immediate attention.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. are a greatest**

 
• The subject in the given sentence is **'climate change' **which is a **singular **subject, hence, the auxiliary verb **'is' **will be used in place of 'are'.
 
• And article **'the'** is used before the **superlative** degree, hence, **'the greatest'** will be used in the given sentence.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **Climate change is the greatest threat facing our planet which needs our immediate attention.**

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

He is __a good singer __of the two.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. the better singer.**

 
• In the given sentence a **comparison** is being made between two persons, hence, **'better' **will be used here.
 
• When we have to **choose one out of two persons** we used the article **'the' **with the comparative degree, hence, **'the better'** will be used.

questions.question:
Identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Great many students who are good at other subjects perform poorly in English.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. Great many students.**

 
• The phrase **'great many' **used in the given sentence is wrong.
 
• The correct phrase is **'a great many' **which is used to refer to **a large number of things or persons.**
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **A great many students who are good at other subjects perform poorly in English.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. This kindness converted his street into a neighbourhood.

B. He and his wife were always ready to lend a helping hand.

C. Mohan was an ideal neighbour in every way.

D. Whether it was lending tools or watering fields, the couple embodied neighbourly kindness
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The correct answer begins with sentence C as it is introducing a subject 'Mohan'.
 
• B & D make paired sentences as sentence B is talking about how kind Mohan and his wife are and their readiness to lend a helping hand. It is continued by sentence D saying they were always ready to help whether it was lending tools or watering fields.
 
• Sentence A is the last sentence as it is giving an overall opinion. 
 
• **Therefore, this sequence is followed by option 1 'CBDA'.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate passive form of the given sentence.

**Please lock the door.**

options.text: You are requested to lock the door.
Please let the door be lock.
You are being ordered to lock the door.
The door should kindly being locked.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• When changing an active sentence into its passive form, the word 'please' changes to 'you are requested to'.
 
• Therefore, only option 1 'You are requested to lock the door' satisfies the rule.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Till quite recently the trend was to go to the west that offered advanced medical facilities.

B. This is because it has on offer the highest level of services, facilities and professional skills.

C. But over the last decade the trend has reversed and India is being chosen for medical tourism.

D. Today, it is not uncommon to travel to a foreign country for medical treatment.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The correct answer does not begin with sentences A, B & C because these sentences begin with prepositions and are dependent on other sentences.
 
• So the sentence begins with D which is talking about how common it is today to travel abroad for medical treatment.
 
• Sentence A & C make paired sentences as sentence A is talking about a trend which is continued by sentence C.
 
• Sentence C is saying that India is being chosen for medical tourism and sentence B is explaining the reason behind that.
 
• **Therefore, this sequence is followed in Option 1 i.e. 'DACB'.**
